key_insight: The segmentation model accurately outlined vertebral artery structures on CTA, but that did not translate into better vertebral artery dissection detection in the reader study.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI-assisted vascular enhancement may be promising for workflow support, but it should not be assumed to improve diagnostic accuracy without further validation.
method: Trained a nnU-Net v2 vascular segmentation model on 101 CTA scans using five-fold cross-validation.
Externally tested the model on 40 CTA scans, including 22 vertebral artery dissection-positive cases.
Ran a 10-reader crossover study comparing CTA interpretation with vs without segmentation-based augmentation.
evidence_signal: The model achieved high segmentation performance (Dice similarity coefficient 0.96 ± 0.01), yet reader accuracy was lower with augmentation than without (0.72 vs 0.84, P < 0.001).
watch_item: High segmentation accuracy did not improve diagnostic performance, so clinical deployment needs caution and more validation in real-world acute settings.
paper_title: Does Deep Learning Vascular Segmentation on CTA Improve Vertebral Artery Dissection Detection?
